name: Introduction and overview — F-15 Eagle — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — F-15 Eagle
description: Introduction and overview of the F-15 Eagle: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The F-15 Eagle is a twin-engine air-superiority fighter built by McDonnell Douglas, entering U.S. Air Force service in 1976. With a combat record of 104 victories to zero losses in air-to-air combat, it is among the most successful fighters ever built. Roughly 1,200 have been produced, including the two-seat F-15E Strike Eagle multirole variant. Baseline facts: Twin-engine air-superiority fighter; USAF service from 1976; ~1,200 built by McDonnell Douglas/Boeing..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
